title: Germany – Asbestos-removal work – Abbruch- und Rückbauarbeiten
description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung sind Schadstoffsanierungsarbeiten im Altbau des Deutschen Technikmuseums Berlin im Zuge der Erneuerung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung. Die Leistungen umfassen die Einrichtung und den Betrieb der Baustelle einschließlich Schwarzbereichen, Personen- und Materialschleusen, Unterdruckhaltungen, Abschottungen, Schutzmaßnahmen sowie erforderlicher Gerüstkonstruktionen für Arbeiten in Installationsschächten und Höhenbereichen. Bestandteil der Leistung sind die Schadstoffsanierung und der Rückbau asbesthaltiger Baustoffe und Bauteile, insbesondere Asbestzementrohre, Brandschutzklappen, Fliesenkleber, Wand- und Deckenbeschichtungen, Brandschutztüren, Rohrflanschdichtungen sowie weiterer asbesthaltiger Bauprodukte. Weiterhin sind KMF-haltige Rohrisolierungen, Dämmstoffe an Lüftungsanlagen, Dämmungen oberhalb von Abhangdecken und in Trockenbaukonstruktionen sowie Hochtemperaturwollen fachgerecht auszubauen. Darüber hinaus sind PCB-haltige Kondensatoren und quecksilberhaltige Leuchtstoffröhren zu demontieren. Die Leistungen beinhalten außerdem Entkernungs- und Abbrucharbeiten, die Herstellung von Schachtöffnungen, die Demontage von Lüftungszentralen, Luftkanälen, Rohrleitungen und sonstigen haustechnischen Anlagenbestandteilen sowie die erforderliche Dekontamination, Grob- und Feinreinigung sämtlicher Sanierungsbereiche einschließlich der Installationsschächte. Ergänzend sind sanierungsbegleitende Messungen, die getrennte Erfassung, Verpackung, innerbetriebliche Logistik, der Transport sowie die ordnungsgemäße Entsorgung gefährlicher und nicht gefährlicher Abfälle einschließlich vollständiger Nachweisführung und Entsorgungsdokumentation auszuführen. Die Arbeiten erfolgen abschnitts- und etagenweise unter laufendem Museumsbetrieb und unter Einhaltung der einschlägigen Anforderungen des Gefahrstoff-, Arbeits- und Umweltschutzrechts.

title: Ertüchtigung KA Kamp-Bornhofen - Los 02
description: Die Kläranlage Kamp-Bornhofen wird von den Verbandsgemeindewerken Loreley betrieben und ist rund 30 Jahre alt. Sie wurde ursprünglich für ca. 1.700 Einwohnerwerte (EW) konzipiert und in Kompaktbauweise innerhalb einer Betriebshalle errichtet. Auf Grundlage aktueller Betriebsdatenauswertungen (2018-2022) liegt die tatsächliche Anschlussgröße bereits bei 2.163 EW. Unter Berücksichtigung geplanter Wohnbau- und Gewerbeentwicklungen wird künftig von einer Belastung von 2.274 EW ausgegangen. Für eine zukunftssichere Auslegung wurde die neue Anlage daher auf 2.700 EW bemessen. Die bestehende Anlage hat ihre hydraulische und stoffliche Leistungsgrenze erreicht. Gleichzeitig wurden seitens der Genehmigungsbehörde verschärfte Einleitbedingungen angekündigt. Insbesondere ist eine Reduzierung des Phosphor-Grenzwertes von derzeit 6 mg/l auf künftig 2 mg/l vorgesehen. Ohne eine grundlegende Ertüchtigung kann die dauerhafte Einhaltung der wasserrechtlichen Anforderungen sowie die weitere Siedlungsentwicklung im Einzugsgebiet nicht gewährleistet werden. Ziel des Vorhabens ist daher die nachhaltige Erweiterung und Modernisierung der Kläranlage zur Sicherstellung der zukünftigen Ausbaugröße, zur Einhaltung der verschärften Einleitwerte sowie zur dauerhaften Verbesserung des Gewässerschutzes im Einzugsgebiet des Rheins. Im Rahmen einer Machbarkeitsstudie wurden mehrere technische Varianten untersucht. Als Vorzugsvariante wurde ein konventionelles Belebtschlammverfahren mit horizontal durchströmter Nachklärung (Variante 1.2) ermittelt. Die geplanten Maßnahmen umfassen insbesondere: - Neubau einer Rechen-Walzensandfang-Kompaktanlage - Neubau eines Belebungsbeckens (ca. 965 m³) - Neubau eines horizontal durchströmten Nachklärbeckens (68 m² Oberfläche) - Neubau eines Schlammstapelbehälters (ca. 310 m³) - Neubau eines Ablaufmessbauwerks - Neubau eines Betriebsgebäudes für Pumpen, Gebläse und Elektrotechnik. (Das Gebäude dient im vorliegenden Fall nicht als klassischer Hochbau, sondern fungiert im Wesentlichen rein als bauliche und funktionale Hülle für die aufzunehmende Maschinentechnik. Gebäudegeometrie und bauphysikalischen Anforderungen werden von den verfahrenstechnischen Parametern der Maschinentechnik vorgegeben.) Die Bemessung erfolgt gemäß DWA-A 131. Die zukünftigen Ablaufwerte erfüllen die verschärften Anforderungen an CSB, BSB5, Stickstoff und insbesondere Phosphor (? 2 mg/l). Besondere Herausforderungen des Projektes sind die Lage im festgesetzten Überschwemmungsgebiet des Rheins, die beengten Grundstücksverhältnisse zwischen Bahnlinie und Bundesstraße sowie die Notwendigkeit der Umsetzung im laufenden Betrieb. Die Baumaßnahme wird daher in mehreren Bauabschnitten realisiert, um die Abwasserreinigung während der gesamten Bauzeit sicherzustellen. Die Maßnahme leistet einen wesentlichen Beitrag zum Gewässerschutz, insbesondere zur Reduzierung der Nährstoffeinträge in den Rhein, und sichert zugleich die kommunale Daseinsvorsorge sowie die weitere städtebauliche Entwicklung der Ortsgemeinde Kamp-Bornhofen.

title: Ireland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – 0055 - The Provision of Security Operations Centre (SOC) and Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Services
description: An Post requires a suitably qualified Security Partner to deliver a managed Security Operations Centre (SOC) and Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) service across its technology estate. The successful Supplier will be responsible for providing a resilient, secure, and professionally managed cybersecurity capability that supports continuous security monitoring, threat detection, incident analysis, alert triage, incident response, escalation management, compliance assurance, service reporting, and ongoing service improvement. The Supplier will work collaboratively with An Post personnel and relevant third-party providers to ensure comprehensive monitoring coverage, effective management of security incidents, and alignment with An Post's security, resilience, governance, and regulatory requirements. The service will include the provision, operation, management, and continuous enhancement of security monitoring and incident management capabilities, including support for Microsoft Sentinel as An Post's current SIEM platform. title: Ireland – Networks – 9719 IM GSM-R Call Monitoring Solution
description: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) currently operates and maintains a national GSM-R mobile network which provides driver to CTC communications via on-board GSM-R cab-mobile equipment provided by Siemens Mobility. Currently, GSM-R is in operation on the DART network, with national rollout expected to occur in 2026 on the rest of IE’s fleets. As part of the overall maintenance of the GSM-R mobile network, IÉ carry out monitoring and drive- testing which at present requires IÉ Telecoms personnel to perform this task. The task requires staff to travel onboard IÉ Trainsets with monitoring equipment, which can be both onerous and time consuming. IÉ require the provision of an automated drive-testing and RF monitoring solution that will negate the requirement for staff to travel. To achieve this requirement, it is therefore required to provide a GSM-R Modem and hardware (option)/software/firmware capable of interfacing with the modem and providing the end-user (IE) with a HTTP REST API. This can be integrated with the existing IÉ hosted servers which run a combination of NodeJS applications, InfluxDB and Grafana for recording and visualization of the obtained data or hosted on a supplier provided cloud-based solution that is accessible by IÉ. Further specific details will be provided to the companies who are pre-qualified to the ITT stage. (This tender was previously issued under Resource ID 7911685, which was cancelled).

title: The Provision of Housing Support Services for Single People and Childless Couples who are Homeless and may have Complex Needs
description: The Service to be provided by the Provider is the provision of a Housing Support Service, primarily for single people or childless couples who are homeless and may have complex needs, residing in supported, interim accommodation. The Provider will also provide or make partnering arrangements with another organisation to provide a Housing Management Service for the accommodation at specific Premises and where applicable will enter into such associated lease arrangements with the owner landlord of the Premises as may be necessary for this purpose. The Housing Management Service does not form part of this Contract but is required to be delivered in conjunction with the Service. Tenderers can determine whether they will provide this service, or whether they will contract with another organisation to provide this service. How this related Housing Management Service is provided will directly impact upon Council budgets for the provision of homeless services and the amount of government funding available to support these services. The Council looks to maximise the monies available to better assist more Service Users. The specific Premises to support the Housing Support Service must be Specified Accommodation as defined by Law. The manner in which the Provider makes formal arrangements for the lease of the Premises will directly impact upon the Council and may result in higher costs to the Council. In respect of any subsidy shortfall however, while the Council cannot mandate how a Provider arranges their commercial business, the Council seeks to maximise the funds available to it to provide appropriate services and to allow maximum recovery, by the Council from the UK Government, of Housing Benefit paid for Service Users assessed as needing Housing Support Services. To assist the Council to maximise recovery of funds Tenderers would require to arrange that they are either (1) a Housing Association, a relevant body in accordance with Regulation 75H of the Housing Benefit Regulations 2006 as amended and enter into the occupancy arrangement (lease between themselves and the Service Users) or alternatively (2) contract with a third party who is a Housing Association and they would enter into lease arrangements with the Service Users and make separate contractual arrangements directly with the Tenderer. Tenderers should be aware that Charities are also relevant bodies for the purpose of the Housing Benefit Regulations 2006, however arrangements made with a Charity would require to be referred to the Rent Officer who would set the amount recoverable, whereas Housing Association arrangements are not subject to this form of review which allows for greater recovery by the Council.

title: Germany – Switchgear – Lieferung einer mobilen Schaltanlage (Leistungsschalteranlagen gasisoliert und metallgekapselt, Sammelschiene 1250 A, 20 kA)
description: Die EAM Netz GmbH (nachfolgend „ENM“) ist ein mittelständischer Strom- und Gasverteilnetzbetreiber. Das ENM-Netzgebiet umfasst eine geografische Fläche von mehr als 11.500 Quadratkilometern und erstreckt sich über weite Teile Hessens sowie über Südniedersachsen, Teile von Ostwestfalen, Westthüringen und seit April 2014 auch über Teile des Landkreises Altenkirchen in Rheinland-Pfalz. ENM versteht sich als Unternehmen mit regionalem Bezug. Die ENM beabsichtig den Kauf einer mobilen Schaltanlage gem. der beigefügten technischen Spezifikation (Anforderung). Lieferung zum frühestmöglichen Zeitpunkt nach Vergabe. Mindestanforderungen: Leistungsbeschreibung Mobile Schaltanlage (Leistungsschalteranlagen gasisoliert und metallgekapselt, Sammelschiene 1250 A, 20 kA): Ausgeschrieben wird eine voll funktionstüchtige Anlage inklusive aller Nebengewerke. Alle im Verfahren nicht genannten Leistungen, die für die Funktionstüchtigkeit notwendig machen, sind Bestandteil und Umfang der Ausschreibung. Der bauliche Teil der mobilen Schaltanlage erfolgt als Containerbauweise. Der Container muss, aus Gründen der Austauschbarkeit bezüglich Abmessungen und Anschlussmöglichkeiten, kompatibel zu den bei EAM Netz vorhandenen mobilen Schaltanlagen sein. Außenabmessungen des Containers LxBxH:7,00x2,54x2,98m und die beigefügten Konstruktionszeichnungen sind zu beachten. 8 Stück MS-Schaltfelder müssen im Container eingebaut werden können. Die gesamte Sekundäranlage inklusive aller Verdrahtungsarbeiten muss erstellt werden. Der Anschluss der Gebäudeinstallation muss hergestellt werden. Im Einzelnen sind anzubieten: • Lieferung und Montage eines 2-Achs-Anhänger in Sonderausführung mit Container oder vergleichbar • Lieferung und Montage einer gasisolierten 24 kV-Mittelspannungsschaltanlage gemäß beiliegender techn. Spezifikation und Übersichtsschaltbild. • Lieferung und Montage der Erdungsanlage • Lieferung und Montage von Grundrahmen und Stahlbaukonstruktion mit zugehöriger Statik • Lieferung und Montage des Doppelbodens • Erstellen einer Druckberechnung für die Nennwerte der Schaltanlage. • Lieferung und Montage eines Druckentlastungssystems falls erforderlich • Erstellen der Rauchschottung • Montage und anschließen aller beigestellten Sekundärschränke inklusive aller Leitungen • Lieferung und Montage der Elektroinstallation inklusive Installationsschrank Die Vergabestelle behält sich vor, den Zuschlag auf Grundlage der Erstangebote gemäß § 15 Abs. 4 SektVO zu erteilen. Sofern hiervon kein Gebrauch gemacht wird, können mit den Bietern Verhandlungen über die preislichen, qualitativen, technischen sowie gegebenenfalls rechtlichen Inhalte ihrer Angebote geführt werden. Im Anschluss erhalten die Bieter Gelegenheit zur Überarbeitung ihrer Angebote. Nach Auswertung der überarbeiteten Angebote kann der Auftraggeber die Anzahl der zur weiteren Verhandlung zugelassenen Bieter reduzieren.

title: The Provision of Housing Support Services for Single People and Childless Couples who are Homeless and may have Complex Needs
description: The Service to be provided by the Provider is the provision of a Housing Support Service, primarily for single people or childless couples who are homeless and may have complex needs, residing in supported, interim accommodation. The Provider will also provide or make partnering arrangements with another organisation to provide a Housing Management Service for the accommodation at specific Premises and where applicable will enter into such associated lease arrangements with the owner landlord of the Premises as may be necessary for this purpose. The Housing Management Service does not form part of this Contract but is required to be delivered in conjunction with the Service. Tenderers can determine whether they will provide this service, or whether they will contract with another organisation to provide this service. How this related Housing Management Service is provided will directly impact upon Council budgets for the provision of homeless services and the amount of government funding available to support these services. The Council looks to maximise the monies available to better assist more Service Users. The specific Premises to support the Housing Support Service must be Specified Accommodation as defined by Law. The manner in which the Provider makes formal arrangements for the lease of the Premises will directly impact upon the Council and may result in higher costs to the Council. In respect of any subsidy shortfall however, while the Council cannot mandate how a Provider arranges their commercial business, the Council seeks to maximise the funds available to it to provide appropriate services and to allow maximum recovery, by the Council from the UK Government, of Housing Benefit paid for Service Users assessed as needing Housing Support Services. To assist the Council to maximise recovery of funds Tenderers would require to arrange that they are either (1) a Housing Association, a relevant body in accordance with Regulation 75H of the Housing Benefit Regulations 2006 as amended and enter into the occupancy arrangement (lease between themselves and the Service Users) or alternatively (2) contract with a third party who is a Housing Association and they would enter into lease arrangements with the Service Users and make separate contractual arrangements directly with the Tenderer. Tenderers should be aware that Charities are also relevant bodies for the purpose of the Housing Benefit Regulations 2006, however arrangements made with a Charity would require to be referred to the Rent Officer who would set the amount recoverable, whereas Housing Association arrangements are not subject to this form of review which allows for greater recovery by the Council.

title: Dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä: Terveydenhuollon hoito- ja yleistarvikkeet
description: Tällä ilmoituksella perustetaan dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä. Hankinnan kohteena dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän (jäljempänä DPS) sisällä olevat perusterveydenhuollossa ja erikoissairaanhoidossa käytettävät hoito-, hygienia- ja yleistarvikkeet, ja tarvittaessa niihin liittyvät lisäpalvelut. HUS pyrkii tällä dynaamisella hankintajärjestelmällä hankkimaan sellaisia perusterveydenhuollon ja erikoissairaanhoidon hoito-, hygienia- ja yleistarvikkeita, joita ei ole huomioitu tällä hetkellä voimassa olevissa hankintasopimuksissa tai joiden tarve on tullut yllättäen muuttuneista tarpeista tai hoitokäytänteistä johtuen. HUS varaa oikeuden järjestää perusterveydenhuollon ja erikoissairaanhoidon hoito-, hygienia- ja yleistarvikkeiden kilpailutuksia tarvittaessa myös tämän dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän ulkopuolella. Hankittavat nimikkeet ja nimikekokonaisuudet määritellään tarkemmin dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisessä kilpailutuksessa. Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän kesto on 48 kuukautta. Pyydämme osallistumishakemuksia perusterveydenhuollossa ja erikoissairaanhoidossa käytettävien hoito-, hygienia- ja yleistarvikkeiden, ja tarvittaessa niihin liittyvien lisäpalveluiden dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään (DPS). Hankinnan kohteena dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän (jäljempänä DPS) sisällä ovat perusterveydenhuollossa ja erikoissairaanhoidossa käytettävät hoito-, hygienia- ja yleistarvikkeet ja tarvittaessa niihin liittyvät lisäpalvelut. Hankittavat nimikkeet ja nimikekokonaisuudet määritellään tarkemmin kussakin dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisessä kilpailutuksessa. HUSin tavoitteena on hankkia joustavalla ja yksinkertaisella menettelyllä laadukkaita perusterveydenhuollossa ja erikoissairaanhoidossa käytettäviä hoito-, hygienia- ja yleistarvikkeita tukemaan HUSin ja sen kumppanien perusterveydenhuoltoa ja erikoissairaanhoitoa. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään voi jättää osallistumishakemuksia koko sen keston ajan. DPS:ään voi hakea tarjoajaksi, jos täyttää soveltuvuusvaatimukset, jotka on ilmoitettu ESPD-lomakkeessa sekä Tarjouspyynnön kohdissa "Muut ehdot" ja "Hankinnan kohteen kriteerit". DPS:ään otetaan mukaan kaikki soveltuvuusvaatimukset täyttävät ehdokkaat. Varsinaiset hankinnat tehdään dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisillä kilpailutuksilla, joissa kuvataan ja täsmennetään hankinnan kohde.

title: Psykososiaalisten menetelmäkoulutusten hankinta
description: Tuomi Logistiikka Oy pyytää Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialueen toimeksiannosta tarjouksia tilaajan henkilökunnalle tarjottavista psykososiaalisista menetelmäkoulutuskokonaisuuksista tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Hankintasopimuksen kohteena ovat Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialueen henkilöstölle järjestettävät psykiatristen häiriöiden psykososiaaliset menetelmäkoulutukset. Koulutukset toteutetaan ammattilaisten työtehtäviä tukevina lyhyt- tai pidempikestoisina koulutuskokonaisuuksina. Menetelmäkoulutusten sisältöön kuuluvat: - Menetelmän teoreettisten periaatteiden ja hoitomallin opetus - Menetelmän rakenteen, vaiheiden ja keskeisten työkalujen läpikäynti - Käytännön harjoitteet, case-esimerkit ja soveltamistavat - Luento-opiskeluun liittyvä koulutusmateriaali: Koulutusmateriaalit ja menetelmään liittyvä opetusmateriaali tulee olla pääosin suomenkielistä. Jos ei suomenkielistä materiaalia ole saatavilla, voi materiaali olla myös englanninkielistä Hankinta on jaettu osa-alueisiin seuraavasti: Osa-alue 1. DKT– Dialektinen käyttäytymisterapia Osa-alue 2. CBASP – Cognitive Behavior Analysis system of Psychotherapy Osa-alue 3. CRT – Cognitive Remediation Therapy Osa-alue 4. SCIT – Social Cognition and Interaction Training Osa-alue 5. START – The Short- Term Assesment of Risk and Treatability Osa-alue 6. KKT – Kognitiivinen käyttäytymisterapia -perusteet Osa-alue 7. Scema Therapy – Skeematerapia Osa-alue 8. MBT – Mentalisation Based Therapy Osa-alue 9. CBT-I, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia Osa-alue 10. HOT, hyväksymis- ja omistautumisterapia Osa-alue 11. BA – Käyttäytymisen aktivaatio Osa-alueiden 1-6 ja 9-11 koulutuskokonaisuudet koostuvat koulutuspäivistä. Osa-alueiden 7 ja 8 koulutuskokonaisuudet koostuvat koulutuspäivistä ja ryhmämuotoisesta työnohjauksesta. Lähikoulutukset ja -tapaamiset toteutetaan tilaajan hallinnoimissa tiloissa tai tilaajan osoittamissa tiloissa. Kaikki tarjouspyynnön mukaiset, soveltuvuusvaatimukset ja palvelua koskevat ehdottomat vähimmäisvaatimukset täyttävät tarjoajat valitaan palveluntuottajiksi. Palveluntuottajista muodostetaan sijajärjestys (=palveluntuottajarekisteri) kokonaistaloudellisesti edullisimman tarjouksen perusteella. Tarjousvertailu ja sijajärjestys muodostetaan osa-alueittain halvimman hinnan perusteella. Sopimuskausi alkaa 1.1.2027 ja on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvo on laskettu koko hankintakokonaisuuden osalta laskennallisen neljän (4) vuoden ajalta perustuen tilaajan arvioimiin asiakasmääriin. Hankintasopimuksen perusteella tehtävien tilausten määrät vaihtelevat tilaajan tarpeen mukaan, eikä hankintasopimus sisällä määrä- tai vähimmäisostovelvoitetta. Hankinnan kohde ja vähimmäisvaatimukset on kuvattu tarjouspyynnössä ja tarjouspyynnön liitteissä. Tarjoaja voi jättää tarjouksen yhteen tai useampaan osa-alueeseen. Rinnakkaisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä., Osa-alue 1. Youngin kehittämä terapiasuuntaus, jossa tutkitaan ja muokataan epätarkoituksenmukaisia skeemoja, jotka saavat ihmisen toimimaan itselleen haitallisella tavalla. Contract Duration: The contract period will be from the date of contract to 2030-03-31 Solicitation Method: Competitive Number of Contracts: One (1) Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement Applies: No Applicable Trade Agreements: The requirement is subject to the provisions of the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP), the Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA), the Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA), the Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement (CColFTA), the Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (CPanFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA), Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) and the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). Requirement Details Tendering Procedure: Selective Tendering This requirement is open only to those TBIPS Supply Arrangement Holders who qualified under Tier 1 for services in the National Capital Region for the following categories: • Category A.1. Application/Software Architect Level 3 • Category I.2. Database Administrator Level 3 • Category I.6. Network Analyst Level 3 • Category I.11. Technology Architect Level 3 The following SA Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: • Accenture Inc. • ADRM Technology Consulting Group Corp. • BoonBridge Corporation • CDW Canada Corp. • CGI Information Systems and Management Consultants Inc. • Cofomo Inc. • Deloitte Inc. • Donna Cona Inc., IBM Canada Limited Joint Venture • Flex Tech Services Inc • Primex Project Management Limited • Prologic Systems Ltd., and Maplesoft Consulting Inc. in JV • Skyfly Solutions Inc., iFathom Corp., EPI-Use Now Inc. in Joint Venture • Spaghetti Logic Inc. • TRM Technologies Inc. • Xelerance Corporation Description of Work: The objective of this requirement is to augment knowledge within the Department of Justice Canada’s (JUS) Cloud team to gather expertise and meet project requirements and specific AI initiatives. The required professional services will support the delivery of key infrastructure components, networking fixes and improvements as well as high visibility projects such as Otto , Artificial Intelligence and the Lakehouse. The Cloud Engineer will implement, configure, automate, and support cloud infrastructure, platform services, and cloud-native solutions in accordance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, enterprise architecture principles, and security controls. The Cloud Engineer will support the deployment, integration, modernization, and operational management of Microsoft Azure services, enterprise applications, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid cloud environments. The Cloud Engineer will collaborate with the Cloud Centre of Expertise (CCoE), Shared Services Canada (SSC), Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to deploy, configure, monitor, troubleshoot, automate, and document cloud services, platform components, application hosting environments, identity services, storage, networking, and operational processes while supporting continuous improvement, operational excellence, and knowledge transfer. The Cloud Architect will design, document, and provide technical leadership for the Department's cloud architecture, ensuring compliance with Government of Canada Cloud Guardrails, departmental standards, security controls, and enterprise architecture principles. The Cloud Architect will support cloud infrastructure, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, Azure platform services, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures. Responsibilities include the design of governance models, subscription hierarchies, landing zones, security architecture, integration patterns, DevSecOps practices, application hosting models, and reference architectures to support enterprise cloud adoption and integration with on-premises and cloud-based services. The Network Specialist will design, implement, document, and support cloud and hybrid networking solutions that provide secure, resilient, and high-performing connectivity between cloud, on-premises, partner, and externally hosted environments. The specialist will support enterprise cloud platforms, cloud-native applications, application modernization initiatives, AI-enabled solutions, and hybrid architectures by designing and implementing networking services, secure integration patterns, and connectivity solutions. The Network Specialist will collaborate with Shared Services Canada (SSC), internal Security Operations, infrastructure teams, application teams, and project stakeholders to design, implement, validate, and document network connectivity, firewall configurations, DNS services, certificate management, identity integration, private connectivity, and network security controls in accordance with Government of Canada standards and departmental policies. The Database Administrator will design, implement, maintain, and optimize database platforms across on-premises and Azure environments, ensuring the availability, performance, security, and recoverability of business-critical systems. The Database Administrator will implement and support backup, restore, high availability, disaster recovery, monitoring, and security controls, while providing technical advice and documentation related to database migrations, cloud integration, and operational best practices in coordination with application teams, Shared Services Canada (SSC), and internal security stakeholders. Bidders must submit a bid for all resource categories. Security Requirement: All Contractor personnel must hold at a minimum, a Personnel security screening level of Reliability. Privileged users require a Personnel Security screening level of Secret. Unscreened personnel are prohibited from performing services under the Contract. Minimum Corporate Security Required: Reliability Minimum Resource Security Required: Secret Contract Authority Name: Ryan Greig Phone Number: 437-295-5631 Email Address: Ryan.Greig@justice.gc.ca Inquiries Inquiries regarding this RFP requirement must be submitted to the Contracting Authority named above. Request for Proposal (RFP) documents will be e-mailed directly from the Contracting Authority to the Qualified Supply Arrangement Holders who are being invited to bid on this requirement. BIDDERS ARE ADVISED THAT “BUYANDSELL.GC.CA” IS NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR THE DISTRIBUTION OF SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language. NOTE: Task-Based Informatics Professional Services (TBIPS) Method of Supply is refreshed three (3) times per year. If you wish to find out how you can be a “Qualified SA Holder”, please contact RCNMDAI.-NCRIMOS@pwgsc.gc.ca

title: Rental of mobile units in the style of construction site trailers, for Canadian Heritage (PCH) events.
description: Description of Requirement: PCH wishes to establish a Standing Offer (SO) agreement with one (1) Contractor for the rental of mobile units, in the style of construction site trailers. These mobile units will be used to meet requirements related to various elements of PCH's event programming (offices, storage area, etc.) in the National Capital Region (NCR). Duration of Contract: The period of the standing offer is from the date of the offer to July 31, 2028 inclusive, with potentially an extension for up to two (2) additional periods of one (1) year each. There are mandatory technical criteria associated with the requirement. For a complete list of all mandatory technical criteria, refer to the solicitation documents. The selection of a successful bidder will be made using the following selection methodology: • Lowest Evaluated Price with Mandatory Technical Criteria. For Canada to declare an offer compliant, the offer must comply with the requirements of the solicitation of offers and meet all mandatory technical evaluation criteria. Canada will consider the compliant offer with the lowest evaluated price for issuance of a standing offer. Security Requirements There are security requirements associated with the resulting contract/standing offer: The following security requirements (LVERS and related clauses, as provided for in the Contract Security Program) apply and form an integral part of the standing offer: 1. The contractor/bidder personnel who require access to regulated worksites* must hold a valid SITE ACCESS STATUS, issued or approved by Canadian Heritage (PCH). 2. Subcontracts which contain security requirements are not to be awarded without the prior written permission of PCH. 3. The contractor/offeror must comply with the provisions of the Security Requirements Check List (SRCL). *NB : The regulated worksite is that of Parliament Hill.

title: Architectural and Engineering Services – New Detachment, Living Quarters, and Outbuilding- South Indian Lake, MB
description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) require the services of an architectural firm (the “Consultant”) together with a multi-disciplinary team of sub-consultants for the provision of services required to deliver the South Indian Lake new detachment, living quarters, and outbuilding. The contract period will be for sixty (60) months from the date of contract. Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation of bids is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. The following security requirements (SRCL, Security Guide and related clauses) apply to and form part of the Agreement. Before the commencement of Work the following conditions must be met: • The Consultant’s personnel are required to be security cleared at the level of Enhanced Reliability Status (ERS) - General Contractor Site Superintendent(s), Project Manager(s), and Mechanical/Electrical sub-trade lead hands must be screened to RCMP ERS. Any other contractors performing work on the facility must be screened to RCMP Facility Access Level 2 (FA2) with Escort, FA2 contractors will have access to sanitized drawings only, as verified by the Personnel Security Unit (PSU) of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). • The Consultant, as well as any subconsultants, must comply with the provisions of the Security Requirements Check List (SRCL) & Security Guide attached at Appendix E. Basis of selection: Highest combined of mandatory and point-rated criteria (80%) and price (20%). Tenders must be submitted by email to: Jeff.Lockyer@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Procuring Office: Jeff Lockyer, RCMP- Procurement and Contracting Branch, Jeff.Lockyer@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. The RCMP has adopted the Ineligibility and Suspension Policy administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada. As a result, the supplier integrity and compliance provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Indigenous Procurement: The federal Indigenous Business Directory (IBD) is an online resource for all levels of government and the private sector to identify Indigenous business capacity. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. A profile in the IBD can also allow you to compete for federal government contracts that are set-aside for Indigenous businesses through the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Businesses. title: Clowes Weir Reconstruction - Rideau Canal National Historic Site of Canada
description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to bid solicitations is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. REQUIREMENT This project entails comprehensive repair of the masonry walls including the upstream wing walls. Secondary project elements include repairs to the concrete apron, and replacement of the steel log gains as well as other structural elements. To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value over & above $5,000,001, Taxes extra. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than May 30, 2028. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT It is recommended that the Bidder or a representative of the Bidder visit the work site. Arrangements have been made for the site visit to be held at Clowes Weir - 495 Heritage Drive, RR4, Merrickville K0G 1N0 on September 18, 2026. The site visit will begin at 10:00 am EDT. Bidders must communicate with the Contracting Authority no later than 48 hours prior, to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders must also complete and submit a certification. Bidders who do not confirm attendance, provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend, or who do not complete and submit the above certification as required will not be allowed access to the site. Bidders will be requested to sign an attendance sheet. No alternative appointment will be given to bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative. Bidders who do not participate in the visit will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than two (2) calendar days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. title: APN_ONTARIO ARMOURIES SITE ENHANCEMENT PROGRAM VARIOUS ONTARIO LOCATIONS
description: Advance Procurement Notice CONSTRUCTION MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR: ONTARIO ARMOURIES SITE ENHANCEMENT PROGRAM VARIOUS ONTARIO LOCATIONS (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity in Hamilton and other locations in Southern and Central Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Description of the Project and Services This project will address infrastructure requirements to recapitalize Department of National Defence reserve and armoury infrastructure at multiple sites throughout Southern and Central Ontario. The delivery method for much of this project is anticipated to be Construction Management. The purpose of this project is to retain the services of a contractor to provide construction management services during the pre-construction and construction phases. The program is anticipated to include planned phased work packages implemented over a 7-10 year period while maintaining operations at the sites. Construction Management services are anticipated to support delivery of Track A (HMCS Star and CFRB Hamilton), are expected to support delivery of Track B (six armouries), and may be expanded in the future to include Track C (thirteen additional armouries). Major construction services are expected to include: Vertical infrastructure; construction of new facilities, recapitalization of existing facilities, and upgrades to building systems and components. Horizontal infrastructure; water distribution, wastewater collection, electrical distribution, communications systems, natural gas distribution, security infrastructure, site services, roads, parking areas and related civil works. The estimated construction cost is in the order of $100,000,000, consisting of approximately $60,000,000 for Track A and $40,000,000 for Track B. Additional future work associated with Track C may increase the overall program value by up to an additional $110,000,000. It is anticipated that this solicitation will be initiated in November 2026. This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by the Department of National Defence (DND). Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, consultants or contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number (Project number on the MERX notice); Contract number 88064; and Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the consultants or contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a consultant or contractor: DCC will  send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or bidder regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent or bidder will need to promptly cooperate with CSP  to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Lucia Apted Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada TTcontracting@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent or bidder agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the bidder or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Open Source Analyst
description: The Office of the Chief Electoral Officer (OCEO), an agent of Parliament, exercises general direction and supervision over the conduct of elections and referendums at the federal level and is commonly known as Elections Canada. title: Design & Construction of the New Accommodations Buildings
description: DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) is requesting Proposals from Design-Build Teams to design and construct the new accommodations buildings at CFB Kingston following a modified design-build approach. The scope of this project is to construct four (4) new accommodations buildings. The initial phase will consist of two (2) buildings with the potential of adding two (2) more buildings subject to approvals. Each building will each consist of a minimum 72 category II rooms in accordance with the DND Living Accommodations with a maximum of six (6) storeys. The scope of work will also include improvements to water, storm, sanitary, power, and telecommunications. A new access road will be required to reach and service these buildings as well as parking. Additional details are provided in the Request for Proposals (RFP) documents. The estimated cost for this opportunity is in the range of $37,600,000 for the two (2) buildings. The overall construction estimate for all four (4) buildings is estimated at $75,200,000. A site visit has been arranged for the following date, time, and location. It is highly recommended that bidders attend this visit. Date: August 27, 2026 Time: 10:00 AM (local time) Location: 3 Radar Street – East Parking Lot, Kingston, ON Firms that consider themselves qualified to provide these services are invited to submit their proposals through the MERX Electronic Bidding System on or before the closing date and time indicated on the Electronic Bidding System. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Chapter Nineteen of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). The selected contractor will be required to hold a valid DESIGNATED ORGANIZATION SCREENING (DOS), issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP) within Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC). Details concerning the Security Requirements for this project are identified in Amendment No.1 to the tender documents. Questions regarding this solicitation are to be directed ONLY to the point of contact identified in this advertisement. Bidders who address their questions to anyone other than the point of contact during the solicitation period may, for that reason alone, be disqualified. Bidders can obtain contract award results from the DCC website at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/contract-activity. DCC now publicly discloses information on payments made to prime contractors so that subcontractors know when they can expect payment. Information on payments made in the past 90 days on construction contracts over $100,000, as well as further information regarding DCC’s prompt payment commitment, can be obtained from the DCC website title: Germany – Planting and maintenance services of green areas – Unterhaltspflege Elbauenpark Magdeburg in 3 Losen
description: Es ist beabsichtigt, die Pflegeleistungen für den Elbauenpark in Magdeburg für einen Zeitraum von einem Jahr (Anlage Plan) unterschiedlicher Größe und unterschiedlichen Leistungsumfanges zu vergeben. Der Auftragnehmer erhält die Option einer Verlängerung des Vertrages um jeweils ein weiteres Jahr bis zu einer Gesamtlaufzeit von maximal 4 Jahren. Der Vertrag verlängert sich jeweils um ein weiteres Jahr, wenn er nicht mit einer Frist von mindestens 12 Wochen zum Ablauf des jeweiligen Vertragsjahres schriftlich gekündigt wird; einer Begründung bedarf es nicht. Einzelheiten der Verlängerungsoption regeln der Bekanntmachungstext und der Vertragsentwurf. Für die Vergütung wird eine Lohnpreisgleitklausel vereinbart; Erhöhungen von Tariflöhnen und gesetzlichem Mindestlohn werden entsprechend berücksichtigt. Es wird ausdrücklich darauf hingewiesen, dass für alle in diesem Leistungsverzeichnis aufgeführten Arbeiten die Beschäftigung von Subunternehmen ausgeschlossen ist (Ausnahme Baumpflege und Inspektion und Wartungskontrolle Spiel - und Sportgeräte nach DIN EN 1176). Vor Kalkulation und Abgabe eines Angebotes wird auf die unbedingt hierfür erforderliche Begehung und Begutachtung des Pflegeobjektes hingewiesen, um sich über die örtlichen Gegebenheiten entsprechend umfassend und ausreichend zu informieren. Nachforderungen die auf Unkenntnis der grundlegenden Situation vor Ort basieren, werden nicht berücksichtigt und zurückgewiesen. Die Arbeiten erfordern Einsatz, Präsenz und Leistungsbereitschaft der Firmen vor Ort (Montag bis Freitag, s. Ausführungen). Die Vorgaben der DIN 18 919 sind Grundlage der Pflegearbeiten im Elbauenpark und werden im Folgenden präzisiert. Für den Bereich des Kleinen Cracauer Angers wurde 2014 ein Pflegehandbuch erstellt. Der Große Cracauer Anger besteht aus 14 einzelnen Pflegebereichen, nach denen die Einteilung der einzelnen Pflegeleistungen und der anteiligen Mengen und Flächen ermittelt wurden. Die Beschreibung der Pflegeleistungen dient als fachtechnischen Pflegegrundlage. Die dargestellten Pflegeintervalle sind ausschließlich Regelannahmen. Das Pflegehandbuch kann in der Verwaltung des Elbauenparks eingesehen werden.

title: France – Electronic components – Fourniture et livraison de composants électroniques pour le Groupe RATP
description: La présente consultation vise à conclure un accord cadre qui porte sur la livraison de composants électroniques pour la RATP : Répartie en deux lots : -Lot 1 : Fournitures de composants électroniques standards -Lot 2 : Fourniture de composants électroniques à approvisionnement complexe Pour chaque lot, le marché qui sera conclu à l’issu de la consultation sera un accord-cadre à bons de commandes mono-attributaire, établi sans montant minimum et avec un montant maximum (+50% du montant médian pour lot 1 / +30% du montant médian pour le lot 2 ). Dans le cadre de cette consultation, la RATP Epic et sa filiale RATP DEVELOPPEMENT ont constitué un groupement pour le lot 1 et pour lequel la RATP a été désignée comme coordonnateur.

The Federal Supply Classification (Product Service Code, PSC) is 1240, Optical Sighting And Ranging Equipment. description: De gemeente Ede wenst de exploitatie van deelauto's in Ede-Centrum en elektrische deelbakfietsen in de hele gemeente Ede in de markt te leggen middels concessies. Met deze concessies beoogt de gemeente een kwalitatief, toekomstbestendig en toegankelijk aanbod van deelauto’s en elektrische deelbakfietsen te realiseren, passend bij de ruimtelijke ontwikkeling van het centrumgebied en de mobiliteitsopgaven van de gemeente. In verband met de verschillende markten en de verschillende concessiegebieden voor deelauto’s en elektrische bakfietsen kiest de gemeente ervoor om deze concessies middels twee aanbestedingen uit te vragen: één voor elektrische deelbakfietsen en één voor deelauto's. Deze aanbesteding betreft de aanbesteding deelauto's. De opdracht betreft de concessie voor de exploitatie van deelauto’s binnen het werkingsgebied van het Mobiliteitsfonds, zoals weergegeven in bijlage 2. De concessie omvat in ieder geval: • de operationele beschikbaarstelling van de deelauto’s • het beheer en onderhoud van de voertuigen; • de klantenservice; • de monitoring en rapportage; • en overige werkzaamheden zoals nader uitgewerkt in het Programma van Eisen.

description: Dublin City Council aims to enhance the quality of life for its residents by developing an integrated Active Travel Network. This comprehensive network is designed to foster connections among individuals via pedestrian pathways, segregated cycle provision and other environmentally friendly transportation alternatives. The enhancement of accessibility and interconnectivity for people walking, wheeling and cycling within this network is anticipated to play a pivotal role in mitigating carbon emissions originating from transport activities. The Council’s objective is to augment the existing 40km network into a seamlessly connected 314km network spanning the entire city. The Gracefield Road to Vernon Avenue Active Travel Scheme is one of the projects identified under this initiative. Gracefield Road, Brookwood Avenue, Sybil Hill Road and Vernon Avenue have been identified as suitable roads for active travel measures. This scheme will deliver protected cycling facilities in both directions and numerous improvements for pedestrians over a 2.6km route along these roads, between the junctions with Malahide Road and Seafield Road. The scheme includes the provision of segregated cycle facilities, improved pedestrian facilities (footpath and junction upgrades), ducting, resurfacing, etc.. The scheme also includes the upgrade of seven signal-controlled junctions to improve pedestrian and cyclist facilities. The scheme comprises the following: - Reconfiguration of existing carriageway for inclusion of protected cycle lanes - Site clearance - Pavement works - Kerbs and footways - Traffic islands - Public lighting - Traffic signs and road markings - Drainage works - Traffic signals and ducting - Utilities - Landscaping and urban realm works - Bike stands - Temporary traffic management. For further information, please refer to documentation available to download from www.etenders.gov.ie; CfT ID 8916766. Please note that this project is subject to funding.

description: Amendment 0005: An amendment has been made to Solicitation W9123626BA0006. Please see attachment SF30, Solicitation Amendment W9123626BA006_0005. The purpose of this project is to construct 24 concrete turning pads, along with required site drainage improvements and road alignment and repair as necessary. The contract will be executed in three distinct phases, with the contractor granted access to only one phase at a time. Completion of each phase is required before proceeding to the next. The remaining phases (two and three) will only be performed if the options for phases are exercised. During construction activities in one phase, the Army will conduct training operations in the remaining two phases. Each turning pad, as identified in the project drawings, will require excavation of the existing roadbed and placement of concrete in accordance with the design specifications. Storm drainage systems will be installed to ensure positive site drainage throughout the construction process. Upon proper curing of the concrete turning pads, the connecting roads will be regarded and aligned to seamlessly integrate with the pads, as detailed in the contract drawings.

description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately 10 years, commencing on or about December 1, 2029, with a right of early termination anytime on or after December 1, 2037 provided written notice is given at least 12 months prior; • approximately 983 usable square metres (um2) of contiguous office space; • approximately 50 um2 of contiguous storage space; basement storage space is preferred; • the proposed space must be available approximately 48 weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. must be within office or commercial type buildings; buildings situated within heavy or medium industrial zoning and industrial type buildings with warehouse or manufacturing space will not be considered. A mixed use building may be considered at the sole discretion of PSPC; 2. proposed space must be contiguous and located entirely on one floor; 3. the dimensions must be compatible for efficient design and use; 4. a minimum floor loading capacity of 10.0 kPa (208.9 lbs. per square foot) for 70 um2 of the above-noted office space requirement; 5. a dedicated telecommunication/equipment room measuring no less than 9.0 um² within the proposed space must be provided; this area will not form part of the Lessee’s usable area noted above but will be included in the rentable area calculation; 6. daytime cleaning must be available; 7. access to a loading area must be available; 8. be fully accessible to persons with a disability; 9. a public transit stop must be within 600 metres of the buildings main entrance, and the frequency of service must not be greater than 30 minute intervals between the hours of 0700 hours and 1800 hours, Monday to Friday inclusive and there must be an accessible walking route between the public transit stop and the building; 10. acceptable space for the installation of a bicycle rack(s); 11. the physical characteristics of the Lands and the Building and the area and environment surrounding it, including neighbouring land uses, shall be compatible with the Lessee’s intended use of the accommodation; • the proposed space must be located in the City of Saskatoon. • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public.

title: SOLE SOURCE � Procurement of Neuron, Linear Accelerator (LINAC) and Combined Environmental Testing Services
description: A solicitation will NOT be posted to https://www.sam.gov due to the sole source nature of this requirement. ITEM DESCRIPTION- Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC), Crane Division, has a requirement and intends to award an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the procurement of Neutron, Linear Accelerator (LINAC), and Combined Environment Testing Services in support of the Radiation Combined Environment Test Capability (RCETC) and military hardware survivability validation programs. The proposed contract action is for the supplies and services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source: Amentum Services Inc., 4800 Westfields Blvd, Ste 400, Chantilly, VA 20151 (CAGE: 5W3V7) under the authority of FAR 6.103-1[JP1] , "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements" (10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1)). The basis for restricting competition is the lack of sufficient technical data, the extreme duplicative cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition, and the unacceptable, mission-critical delays in fulfilling the agency's requirements through any other source. To sustain reliable, technically advanced nuclear weapon effects (NWE) simulation testing without duplicating massive prior Government investments in pre-project planning, hosting solution design, and facility systemization, the Contractor must possess immediate, turn-key site and operational readiness. Specifically, the only source capable of satisfying this requirement must possess: Secured Real Estate: Existing secured real estate located within immediate proximity to NSWC Crane, Indiana, to support physical GFE delivery, secure handling, and immediate logistical integration. 100% Completed Facility Designs: Completed and Government-approved facility architectural/engineering (A/E) designs (including civil, structural, mechanical/electrical utilities, and verified radiation shielding calculations) optimized to house the Government-Furnished Property (GFP). Advanced Regulatory & Safety Bases: Completed and mature Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) license applications, Indiana Department of Health (IDoH) device registrations, Hazard and Operability Studies (HAZOP), and finalized Safety Basis/Radiological Control program documentation tailored explicitly to the safe operation of the high-intensity simulator sources. Established GFE Vendor Integration: Matured coordination, transition planning, and technical exchanges with the GFE manufacturer (Verus Research) to support immediate systemization, Operational Site Acceptance Testing (OSAT), and long-term capability sustainment. The contractor will be responsible for the end-to-end operation, availability, maintenance, and enhancement of NSWC-owned NWE simulators (specifically the Dense Plasma Focus (DPF) and Electron Linear Accelerator (LINAC) systems), associated diagnostics, and other GFP. No other source possesses the requisite specialized facility infrastructure, site readiness, and technical safety/regulatory baseline to perform these efforts immediately upon award. Any attempt to re-initiate the facility design, licensing, and systemization processes with another vendor would result in an unacceptable delay of multiple years and a substantial, non-recoverable duplication of cost to the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement or proposal which shall be considered by the agency. However, a determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this solicitation is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of re-evaluating the justification for sole source or limitation of sources and making a determination to change the acquisition strategy to a competitive procurement. The Solicitation and amendments for this sole source action will not be posted to sam.gov and are available only from the POC identified below. Request for Proposal (RFP) will not be made available through https://www.sam.gov. The RFP will be provided to directly to Amentum through electronic mail. The proposed noncompetitive contract action is anticipated to be awarded under FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiations. Contractors must be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the internet at https://www.sam.gov. Questions or inquiries should be directed to Jamie Wilson, Code: 0233, Jamie.k.wilson1.civ@us.navy.mil. Please reference the above solicitation number when responding to this notice.

title: Request for Information (RFI) for Silent Anvil Air-Launched Torpedo (SAA-LT) Standoff Delivery Solutions
description: DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION. THE GOVERNMENT MAY USE THE INFORMATION RECEIVED TO INFORM A POTENTIAL PROTOTYPE PROJECT UNDER OTHER TRANSACTION AUTHORITY (OTA), PURSUANT TO 10 U.S.C. � 4022. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. ALL INFORMATION SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS RFI IS VOLUNTARY AND THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT COMPENSATE ANY RESPONDENT FOR ANY COST INCURRED IN DEVELOPMENT OF INFORMATION PROVIDED TO THE GOVERNMENT. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL; YET IS A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL TO DETERMINE POTENTIAL FIRMS CAPABLE OF PROVIDING THE SUPPLIES DESCRIBED HEREIN PRIOR TO AN ISSUANCE OF A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THE GOVERNMENT IS NOT OBLIGATED TO PAY FOR ANY INFORMATION RECEIVED FROM POTENTIAL SOURCES AS A RESULT OF THIS RFI. THIS DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT OF ANY KIND. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT OR NON-FAR BASED AGREEMENT (E.G. OTHER TRANSACTION) AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IN RESPONSE TO THIS RFI IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. FAILURE TO SUBMIT A RESPONSE WILL NOT PREVENT A COMPANY FROM PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE COMPETITION RELATED TO PMX-201'S SILENT ANVIL PROGRAM. CLASSIFICATION OF RESPONSES: ALL SUBMTTED INFORMATION PROVIDED MUST BE UNCLASSIFIED. ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION SUBMITTED MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED AS SUCH AND WILL BE SAFEGUARDED IN ACCORDANCE WITH APPLICABLE GOVERNMENT REGULATIONS. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED MAY BE REVIEWED AND USED ACROSS THE GOVERNMENT. The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of Strike Weapons Program Office (PMX-201), is seeking to determine industry�s capabilities to design, develop, test, and fabricate cost-effective, rapid prototyping alternatives for the of the Silent Anvil Air-Launched Torpedo (SAA-LT). SAA-LT is a next-generation Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) standoff delivery system being developed by the U.S. Navy to address emerging threats in undersea warfare. It is designed to expand the range of manned and unmanned aircraft platforms capable of executing ASW missions. SAA-LT will be captive-carried and released from both internal and external aircraft weapons stations utilizing standard Department of War (DOW) carriage systems. SAA-LT will operate as a precise and highly maneuverable glide weapon, transitioning quietly to target areas to engage enemy submarines from distance. Prototyping Objectives & Timeline Demonstration: Demonstrate an end-to-end prototype capability of the SAA-LT system within eighteen (18) months of agreement award Fabrication: Rapidly assemble and deliver approximately one hundred eighty (180) prototype all-up-rounds (AURs) within the three (3) years following the successful end�to-end demonstration. Acquisition Pathways The Navy is exploring two parallel design options and invites industry partners to respond to Option 1, Option 2, or both: Design Option 1 (End-to-End Solution): A complete, integrated SAA-LT solution from aircraft separation to the underwater target. Design Option 2 (Wing Kit Standoff Design): An unpropelled glide wing kit configured to carry a Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) / Government Furnished Information (GFI) effector (torpedo) to the target area. The Government is considering utilizing the Naval Air Systems Consortium (NASC) to potentially award one or more OTAs pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 4022 �Authority of the Department of Defense to carry out certain prototype projects�.
